outline.chapter_title: 1️⃣ Introductory to Tabular Learning and Its Foreground in Industry
outline.description: Grounds the reader in why tabular data is ubiquitous in real‑world settings such as finance and healthcare and outlines traditional supervised models alongside their limitations when labeled samples are scarce.
subtopics: Characteristics of tabular datasets (heterogeneous types, missing values)
Standard supervised pipelines (LogReg, tree‑based) and their high‐data demands
The growing need for data‑efficient techniques when annotation costs are prohibitive

outline.description: Introduces the few‑shot setting mathematically and reviews core ideas used across modalities while highlighting what makes tabular data uniquely challenging.
subtopics: Formal definition of k‑shot training sets
General strategies – data augmentation, self‑supervision and unsupervised pre‑training
Why generic augmentations struggle on table schemas

outline.description: Explains the scale, architecture and training regime under which LLMs acquire extensive world knowledge and prompting tricks needed for downstream tasks.
subtopics: Transformer backbone and autoregressive training on text corpora
The rise of chain‑of‑thought reasoning signals
Evidence that LLMs encode scientific‐style domain facts usable beyond language

outline.chapter_title: 4️⃣ Prior Efforts in LLM‑Based Tabular Learning
outline.description:
Survey existing paradigms converting tables to natural language prompts then feeding them into an LLM.
Critiques focus on inference latency, required fine‑tuning hooks and prompt size ceiling.
